channel.title: Why Do We Need AI
channel.description: Practical AI guides and documented experiments for small-business owners.

item.title: How to avoid AI workslop that wastes your reader’s time
item.description: AI can make unfinished thinking look finished. Before sending a draft, check whether your reader has the facts, decisions and next steps they need.

item.title: How Can Customers Find Your Small Business on ChatGPT?
item.description: Make your services clear, check crawler access and try realistic searches. Practical steps for small-business owners, without promises of guaranteed recommendations.

item.title: ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini: which one is best at what
item.description: Our picks, job by job: Claude for long documents, ChatGPT for numbers and images, Gemini or Copilot for everyday office work. Researched, not tested.

item.title: Turn last month's bank statement into a budget you'll actually keep
item.description: Holiday spending starts this month. Strip out the personal details, paste in one statement, and get a budget built on how you actually spend.

item.title: Hosting Thanksgiving? One prompt gets you the menu, the timeline and the grocery list
item.description: Give ChatGPT four facts about your kitchen and ask for a menu, an hour-by-hour plan and one grocery list sorted by aisle. Then check the turkey against USDA.

item.title: Can AI type your invoices into a spreadsheet?
item.description: We ran 24 invented invoices, including scans and handwriting, through an AI model and a rules script. AI read messy ones better but missed a bad total.

item.title: AI vs. simple rules for appointment and payment reminders
item.description: We ran 30 made-up reminder records through a rules script and an AI model three times each. Rules got every routine case right.

item.title: We ran 30 invented customer inquiries through an AI follow-up assistant
item.description: A 30-case synthetic test: stop checks passed, but one draft made unapproved promises.

item.title: We tested our AI readiness checklist on 12 made-up workflows
item.description: We ran our readiness checklist on 12 invented workflows. It's a good brake and a poor compass.

item.title: Small-business lead follow-up automation: a blueprint
item.description: A lifecycle map for capture, handoff, follow-up, and closure, with exceptions and stop conditions to write first.

item.title: AI agents are moving into your business apps
item.description: Use an Agent Action Contract and a contractor test plan to decide what an assistant may read, draft, propose, and change.

item.title: How to evaluate an AI pilot: keep, fix, or stop
item.description: Use a pilot evidence sheet, quality buckets, net-time math, and a worked example to decide whether an AI workflow deserves to continue.

item.title: What data should you put into an AI tool?
item.description: Use a green-yellow-red data framework and a pre-upload checklist before business information enters an AI workflow.

item.title: How to calculate the ROI of AI automation
item.description: Use a conservative five-number model to calculate net monthly value, break-even volume, and payback period.

item.title: AI vs. automation: when your small business actually needs AI
item.description: Use the Minimum Intelligence Principle and a four-question decision test to choose between rules, AI, and human judgment.

item.title: 5 tasks your small business should automate before anything else
item.description: Use a five-question scorecard, simple ROI math, and a worked example to identify repetitive work worth automating.

item.title: The small-business AI readiness checklist
item.description: Score one workflow with a 20-point readiness check and turn the result into a one-page pilot brief.

item.title: How to choose your first AI tool without wasting money
item.description: Compare tools with the same real work, a 35-point scorecard, total-cost math, and a 30-day pilot.
